record_title: Random linear syndromes attain the all-rate Renyi guesswork exponent
provenance: Extends recent constrained-guesswork results for random linear codes by replacing weight-spectrum analysis with a source-independent collision-moment theorem for uniform random linear syndrome maps, and connects the resulting exponent to classical Renyi guesswork/task-encoding converses.
limitations: The field size q is fixed; constants are not claimed uniform for growing q. The theorem concerns optimal likelihood-ordered guessing within syndrome classes and does not provide an efficient ordering algorithm. It establishes the leading exponential rate rather than the sharp logarithmic second-order term. Originality is to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from adjacent universal-hashing and random-binning literature.
